title: A first collaboration between The Gauchers Association and INPDA

sentences.text: We support families affected by Gaucher disease; INPDA supports families affected by acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD, Niemann-Pick A/B).
Both diseases involve missing enzyme activity and fatty substances building up in cells’ recycling compartments, called lysosomes.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that comparison has confidence 0.48, below 0.5, so it needs careful checking.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The Registry of Patients Diagnosed With Lysosomal Storage Diseases and the Institutional Registry of Rare Diseases both include Gaucher disease.
We propose comparing their approaches to collecting information, rather than assuming their data or participation arrangements can transfer across diseases.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: The deficient enzymes and stored substances differ between Gaucher disease and ASMD.

Please help check whether short horizontal eye movements, raised blood glucosylsphingosine and reduced beta-glucocerebrosidase also occur in ASMD, rather than treating missing records as proof of absence.
Before combining information, we should also review the brain-disease evidence and how to represent GBA1’s role in Parkinson disease.

This month, we propose sending INPDA one inquiry asking whether the National Multicentre Study of the Natural History of Acid Sphingo-myelinase Deficiency in Adults and Children could include Gaucher disease.

What published evidence could we discuss with a neurologist about addressing brain disease in Gaucher types 2/3, ASMD type A, MPS I Hurler and neuronopathic MPS II, separately from effects on the body?
How should GBA1’s role in Parkinson disease be represented?
Which GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA variants might respond to protein-stabilising approaches, and how could they be classified as GLA variants are?
I am writing on behalf of The Gauchers Association to propose a small shared inquiry.
Our diseases share enzyme deficiency and storage within lysosomes.
Could you help us ask whether the natural-history study named above could include Gaucher disease?
We would welcome your guidance on what needs checking first.
Thank you for considering this proposal.
[Your name], on behalf of The Gauchers Association
